brief: Dietrich Bonhoeffer, born in 1906, is remembered for his determined opposition to National Socialism and for his courageous suffering and death at the hands of the Gestapo on 9 April 1945. He was convinced that religion must be central to life and explored ways of talking about God in secular language as “the beyond in the midst”, even when this meant freeing Christianity from the strictures of traditional religion. His own life in captivity bore eloquent testimony to his belief that “it is the fellowship of the cross to experience the burden of the other.”
